card: Allows Bitcoin Core nodes to run txindex concurrently with block pruning if the index has no legacy entries. When a requested transaction is in a pruned block, RPC and REST error responses return candidate block hashes so callers can fetch them on demand via getblockfrompeer and retry. Additionally, getrawtransaction verbosity 2 omits fee and prevout data instead of failing when undo data is absent for refetched blocks. Resolves four long-standing feature requests dating back to 2017 (#10609, #12651, #16182, #35240).
changed_since_previous: No substantial changes in approach or commit structure since the previous revision.
evidence: PR description: 'After #35531, each txindex entry now points to the block hash containing the tx instead of the file location of the block... This allows us to determine the hash of the containing block even if the block is later pruned'
problem: Nodes running with pruning cannot maintain or query a txindex, forcing anyone who needs txindex lookups or RPCs like getrawtransaction and gettxoutproof to store the full raw block history on disk.

risk.why: Mistakes in index pruning checks or error reporting could cause RPC or REST callers to receive false transaction misses or fail to locate transactions during chain reorganizations.

scope_notes: Touches txindex lookup paths and introduces a new TxLookupResult return variant in src/node/tx_lookup_result.h; updates JSONRPCError to take optional structured error data returned under error.data.
summary: Enables the transaction index (-txindex) to run on pruned nodes as long as the index contains no legacy format entries. When a lookup in txindex points to a pruned block, GetTransaction and related interfaces return the candidate block hashes so callers can fetch the missing blocks with getblockfrompeer. It also updates getrawtransaction verbosity 2 to gracefully omit fee and prevout data instead of throwing an error when undo data is unavailable.
